newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seeks to stabilise above 4,000 points.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seeks to stabilise above 4,000 points.

text.p: Germany's DAX index took a real beating on Monday, falling as much as four percent at one point, but market analysts and dealers believe the market's dramatic advance so far this year remains intact.
The blue-chip DAX index, catching up to Friday's Wall Street slump, ended bourse trade on Monday down 74.26 points at 4,078.60 points after falling as low as 3,976.67 points in volatile dealings.
The index was steady in post-bourse IBIS computer dealings, trading up 8.71 points at 4,086.30 points, as traders said the market was seeking to find some footing above 4,000 points.
The dramatic drop since Friday, tied to the weak dollar and Wall Street losses, knocked some of the shine off the DAX's 55 percent rise so far in 1997 to a high at 4,477.70 points.
But many believe the DAX will soon resume posting gains and keep outperforming the U.S. market, where the Dow Jones index has risen less than 30 percent so far this year.
"We assume that we will see a market course that will put the DAX at about 4,700 points within nine to 12 months," said Christoph Benner at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Frankfurt.
Major factors supporting the German market include the mark still remaining relatively weak against the dollar.
Also helping the market are few prospects for the Federal Reserve or the Bundesbank to take any action soon on raising interest rates, which could weigh on corporate profits.
Still, some dealers said the German share market may not yet have found a solid foundation at the moment and could remain vulnerable to movements in the Dow Jones index.
"The DAX should spend the week bouncing around 4,000 points," said Ingo Mainert at Commerzbank in Frankfurt.
Mainert said there was no similarity between the market's rocky condition now and the 1987 market crash.
"We are merely seeing a correction after the historically high levels we have reached, just as occurred in 1986 and 1994," he said, noting other market corrections that occurred before fresh gains.

Among specific shares, carmaker Volkswagen AG was up 21 marks at 1,274 marks in post-bourse dealings after reporting a 73 percent rise in group net profit to 488 million marks along with a bright outlook for the rest of 1997.
Other carmakers were mixed as BMW AG rose one mark to 1,300 marks, while Daimler-Benz AG was down 80 pfennigs at 136.05 marks.
